profile.campus: Ashburn, Loudoun County, Virginia (Equinix Ashburn campus, Data Center Alley)
profile.address: 21701 Filigree Court, Building D, Ashburn, VA 20147
profile.reading:
This building operates as Equinix's DC5 data center at 21701 Filigree Court, Building D, in Ashburn, Virginia, one node in Equinix's cluster of buildings spread across Loudoun County's Data Center Alley. Equinix's own DC5 facility page publishes concrete numbers rather than general marketing text, 57,544 square feet of space, N+2 power redundancy on its UPS system, N+1 block redundant generator configuration rated for 30 hours or more at full load, a cooling redundancy Equinix lists as N+20 percent, a figure distinct from the flat N+1 or N+2 cooling ratios Equinix publishes for several sibling buildings nearby, a one story reinforced concrete building rated for 200 psf floor load with double interlock pre-action fire suppression, and nine compliance certifications, HECVAT, HIPAA, ISO 9001, ISO 22301, ISO 27001, NIST 800-53/FISMA High, PCI DSS, SOC 1 Type II, and SOC 2 Type II. Equinix does not publish an IT load or utility power figure in megawatts for DC5 itself, so this entry does not assign one.

Ashburn's status as the center of Data Center Alley predates Equinix's arrival. AOL built what is generally regarded as the area's first data center, its Dulles Technology Center, in 1997 to support its dial up internet subscriber base, and the fiber capacity that project pulled into Loudoun County helped seed the cluster of interconnected facilities that followed. Equinix opened its own first Ashburn building, DC1, in the late 1990s, and its second building, DC2, earned a reputation, per Data Center Dynamics, as one of the most connected buildings on earth. Loudoun County's data center corridor has since grown into what Data Center Dynamics describes as roughly 10 million square feet of built space consuming on the order of 1 gigawatt of electrical power region wide, a figure covering every operator in the corridor rather than Equinix alone.

Equinix's own Washington D.C. metro listing page currently names and links 15 facilities together, DC1 through DC6, DC10 through DC16, DC21, and DC22, with most addresses in Ashburn and at least one, DC14, in nearby Manassas. Equinix does not publish a combined power or square footage total for that group of buildings, and Equinix markets DC1 through DC6 and DC10 through DC12 collectively as offering access to one of the top three internet peering exchange markets on the East Coast, without singling out DC5's own peering density or customer roster.

Every data center on this campus now also sits inside Virginia's evolving electricity regulatory framework for large power users. The State Corporation Commission approved new Dominion Energy rates in November 2026 that raise a typical residential bill by about 16 dollars a month, while creating a new GS-5 rate class specifically for data centers, effective January 1, 2027, that requires large demand customers like Equinix's Ashburn buildings to sign 14 year minimum contracts with cost coverage guarantees, according to Inside Climate News's reporting on the commission's decision.

reading.body:
Equinix DC5 is a 57,544 square foot building at 21701 Filigree Court in Ashburn, Virginia, one of 15 linked facilities Equinix operates across Loudoun County without publishing a combined power capacity for the group. The building holds N+2 power redundancy on its UPS system, an N+1 block redundant generator configuration, and an unusual N+20 percent cooling redundancy distinct from the N+1 or N+2 ratios Equinix publishes for nearby sibling buildings. No IT load or utility power figure in megawatts is published for DC5 itself, so its absolute capacity cannot be compared to other facilities.

The facility qualifies to host healthcare data under HIPAA, financial systems under PCI DSS and SOC 1/2 compliance, federal government workloads under NIST 800-53/FISMA High classification, and business continuity operations under ISO 22301. Equinix does not disclose DC5's specific customer roster or peering density, though it markets DC1 through DC12 collectively as providing access to one of the three highest-traffic internet exchange points on the US East Coast.

Ashburn's Data Center Alley concentrates roughly 10 million square feet of operational data center space across all operators, consuming on the order of 1 gigawatt of power region-wide. Virginia's State Corporation Commission approved new Dominion Energy rates effective January 1, 2027, creating a GS-5 rate class that requires data centers like Equinix's Ashburn buildings to sign 14 year minimum contracts with cost coverage guarantees, embedding long-term power commitments into the operating structure of the region's largest single cluster of AI-capable colocation space.
